Erin: Heads-up — ACME (org_acme_id=acme-42) reporting a surge of indexing failures after yesterday's embed model swap. ~25% of inserts getting rejected by the indexer with a vector-shape error. Also seeing increased latency / some 429s from the embeddings endpoint for that org. Sample error from indexer log:

```
ERROR idx-insert: vector_shape_mismatch: expected=1536 got=1024 doc_id=acme-12345 request_id=req-9a8b7c
```

I opened a support ticket and customer is blocked for searches. Can eng runtime + indexing triage? ETA needed and customer-facing mitigation please.

Kai: thanks Erin. Do we know which embedding model they were routed to? Full request payload or sample curl? Any router overrides for acme?

Erin: They were routed to `redwood-embed-large-v2` after the default catalog update. Repro curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-v2","input":["hello world"]}'
```

Response includes "embedding": [ ... ] length 1536. Indexer expects 1024. Also attaching small batch log where some docs succeeded (old ones) and some failed.

Kai: ok that matches — model swap increased dim from 1024->1536. Our indexer schema for ACME is pinned at 1024 vectors. Two paths: rollback routing for acme to previous embed model OR add a migration/backfill to re-ingest with 1536-dim vectors (or store 1536 in a new column). Quick mitigation is to rollback the model mapping for that org. Longer term we need a migration strategy.

Luca: from indexer side — vector DB (third-party) enforces fixed dimension per collection. We can't accept mixed-dim inserts. Current options:
- Reject new dims (status quo)
- Create a new collection for 1536 and gradually backfill + swap reads (complicated for ACME)
- On-the-fly down-project 1536->1024 with PCA-ish transform (risky for quality)

For immediate recovery I recommend rollback routing + a controlled backfill run into a new collection. We'll need a migration plan that preserves IDs and handles aliasing.

Devon: SRE notes embedding endpoint latency spike correlated with bigger model usage and larger batch memory pressure. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/embeds/acme?from=now-6h shows median p95 latency up ~220ms and some 429s. Current batch config for hosted endpoint is target_batch_size=128, max_wait_ms=40. For larger vectors that increases GPU memory and reduces throughput. Two quick actions: lower target_batch_size to 32 for acme tenant or pin acme to dedicated pool if they need high qps.

Ingrid: Oncall — please do the rollback routing for the org now. Also add an indexer-safe stopgap: transform 1536->1024 by truncation (zero-pad -> truncate) only as a temporary emergency if rollback isn't possible. Document risk to vector similarity. I'll coordinate with legal/support for customer comms.

Erin: I'll tell the customer we're rolling back the embed model routing and that eng is preparing a migration/backfill plan. Can someone post the rollback command?

Kai: rollback command for router CLI:
```
redwood-router set-route --org acme-42 --service embeddings --model redwood-embed-small-v1 --reason "support: rollback after dim mismatch" --by erin
```
I've queued the change; ops-bot will post when deployed.

ops-bot: Deploy started: router-change id=deploy-773a status=running by Kai

ops-bot: Deploy succeeded: router-change id=deploy-773a status=ok at 1717777890

Erin: Confirmed with ACME — new inserts successful and indexer rejections dropped to 0%. Thanks.

Luca: I'll draft migration runbook: create new collection acme_vectors_v2 (1536), backfill from source using stable snapshot, run A/B reads for 24h, then swap alias. Will coordinate timing with ACME and SRE.

Devon: I'll also apply a tenant-specific batch cap for ACME to protect other tenants: target_batch_size=32 for org=acme-42, effective immediately.

Ingrid: Assigning postmortem owner to Luca. Please include root cause (catalog auto-swap), mitigations, runbook for migrations, and an RBAC check so only ent-level orgs get auto-upgraded models.

Erin: Filed support ticket #SUP-12345, added ACME notes and shared rollback summary. Customer ok for a scheduled migration window tomorrow.

Kai: Follow-ups: add a preflight check in the router that compares model.dim -> indexer.collection_dim for pinned orgs and block auto-upgrades when mismatch. I'll open an RFC.

ops-bot: Incident note created: incident-2024-emb-dim-172 (labels: embeddings, indexer, customer-impact)

Erin: Closing triage — thanks all. We'll keep thread updates in ticket SUP-12345.
